source.states: ReceiptEdit US State Sales Tax Dataset 2026.1 (https://github.com/receiptedit/us-sales-tax-2026), last updated 2026-06-17, MIT. District of Columbia 6.00% statewide rate from the DC Office of Tax and Revenue.
source.zips: DeepCalc US sales-tax ZIP table (https://deepcalc.com/data/us-sales-tax/zip), dominant combined rate; primarily 2026 Q3 (Ohio 2026 Q1, Iowa 2025 Q3, Nevada 2025 Q4). Only ZIPs that differ from the state base rate are stored.
source.prefixes: USPS ZIP Code prefixes via alecperkins/zip-state (CC0). Prefixes 202-205 are mapped to DC (USPS unique/government ZIPs).
source.vehicle: Official state DMV/DOR pages and statutes, corroborated by the Pennsylvania DOR Sales and Use Tax Credit Chart (REV-227, updated 2026-09-12). These are motor-vehicle titling/excise/highway-use rates, not general retail sales-tax rates. Vehicle-rate table as of 2026-11.

notes.text: Alabama taxes motor vehicles at a 2% state rate (general sales tax is 4%); local rates still apply. Estimated as the combined general rate minus 2 percentage points.
Delaware has no sales tax. The DMV document fee is 5.25% of purchase price (effective October 1, 2025).

DC excise tax is 1%–11% of fair market value by unladen weight and city MPG (electric vehicles 1%–3%), effective February 17, 2025. 6.00% is a mid-range estimate (3,500–4,999 lb, 21–25 MPG). Enter the rate for this vehicle.
Florida state rate is 6%. County discretionary sales surtax applies only to the first $5,000 and is not included in this estimate (at most about $75).
Georgia charges a 7% Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) in place of sales tax. No local sales tax on the title.
Iowa exempts motor vehicles from sales tax and charges a 5% fee for new registration.
Indiana charges a 7% statewide rate on motor vehicles; local sales tax does not apply.
Kentucky charges a 6% motor vehicle usage tax statewide; local sales tax does not apply.
Maryland charges a 6.5% vehicle titling excise tax (general sales tax is 6% and does not apply).
Minnesota motor vehicle sales tax is 6.875%. Local sales tax does not apply. A few cities levy a separate local vehicle excise tax that is not included.
Some Minnesota cities levy a separate local vehicle excise tax that is not included in this estimate.
Mississippi taxes motor vehicles and light trucks (10,000 lbs or less) at 5% (general sales tax is 7%).
Different rates apply to heavier trucks and some other vehicles; not modeled.
North Carolina charges a 3% highway use tax in place of sales tax.
A $2,000 cap applies only to Class A/B commercial motor vehicles and recreational vehicles, not to typical cars, SUVs, or light trucks.
North Dakota charges a 5% motor vehicle excise tax in place of sales tax.
New Mexico charges a 4% motor vehicle excise tax (not the gross receipts tax).

OK.name: motor vehicle excise and sales tax

notes.text: Oklahoma charges 3.25% motor vehicle excise tax plus 1.25% sales tax (4.50% combined). Local sales tax does not apply.
South Carolina charges a 5% infrastructure maintenance fee in place of sales tax, capped at $500.
South Dakota charges a 4% motor vehicle excise tax (general sales tax is 4.2%).
Texas charges a 6.25% motor vehicle sales tax. Local sales tax does not apply to motor vehicles.
Vermont charges a 6% purchase and use tax on automobiles and light trucks.
A $2,486 cap applies to heavy trucks (curb weight 10,100 lbs or more) and some other vehicles, not typical cars or light trucks.
West Virginia charges a 6% statewide titling sales tax. Local sales tax does not apply.
A flat $30 titling tax applies when the net purchase price is under $500; not modeled.
Connecticut charges the 6.35% state rate on motor vehicles; there is no local sales tax.
A 7.75% rate may apply to vehicles priced over $50,000; not modeled. Enter the rate by hand if it applies.
